summary: Close the GN.0 follow-up at target level by importing its accepted metric-lattice foundations and planning the integral saturation, maximal-minor content, exact-kernel and congruence-kernel consequences routed from Browning–Le Boudec–Sawin. All covolumes use intrinsic Euclidean volume. The consumer-owned weighted number-field normalization has an accepted supplier plan; it is not reconstructed here.

nodes.title: Coordinate saturation
nodes.statement: For L≤A_N, sat(L) is the inverse image in A_N of span_Q(L) under coordinate cast to Q^N. Call L primitive when sat(L)=L.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: Use the native rational span, restrict scalars to Z and take the native comap along coordinate cast. This is a concrete wrapper, not a new finite-free module or general torsion-free quotient theory.
Containment and monotonicity follow from span. Applying span twice proves idempotence. The next comparison theorem proves the integral-denominator and real-span descriptions.

nodes.title: Rational, integral and real descriptions of saturation
nodes.statement: For every L≤A_N and x∈A_N, x∈sat(L) iff there is a nonzero integer m with mx∈L, and iff the real coordinate vector of x belongs to span_R L. Consequently sat(L) has the same rank and real span as L.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: Apply exists_smith_normal_form_of_le to L≤A_N. In an integral ambient basis L is generated by a_i b_i for i<r; independence of the L basis implies each a_i≠0.

An integral basis of A_N has unimodular coordinate matrix; casting it to Q and R gives a basis in each field. Thus both rational and real membership are vanishing of the coordinates outside the initial r positions.

For an integral vector with those coordinates zero, the product of the nonzero a_i clears all denominators, including the empty product 1 when r=0. Conversely a nonzero integer scalar is invertible over both fields.
The first r ambient vectors span the saturation and both field spans, proving rank agreement without importing or reproving the general direct-summand dictionary.

sources.match: Worker comparison between the source real-span convention and the concrete rational-coordinate definition.

acceptance: For L=Z(2,2), (1,1) has denominator witness m=2.
For L=0, only the zero vector has a nonzero scalar multiple in L.

nodes.title: Integral orthogonal rank and double orthogonal
nodes.statement: Use the existing integral orthogonal submodule L⊥ for the coordinate dot product. For every L≤A_N, L⊥ is primitive, rank_Z(L⊥)+rank_Z(L)=N, and (L⊥)⊥=sat(L). Its real span is (span_R L)⊥.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: Integer dot-product equations survive division by a nonzero integer, so the denominator criterion makes L⊥ saturated.

Apply the parent orthogonal-intersection-basis to the standard self-dual lattice Z^N and the rational real span of L, using saturation-characterisation to supply the full intersection. This gives a full intrinsic lattice in the real orthogonal subspace.
Use the pinned complementary-dimension identity for the rank sum. Apply the pinned real double-orthogonal identity and saturation-characterisation to obtain (L⊥)⊥=sat(L).

sources.match: States primitive orthogonals, complementary rank and the primitive double-orthogonal criterion.
Explains full rank by rational orthogonal equations.

nodes.title: Exact dot-product kernel
nodes.statement: For c∈A_N let K(c)=ker(x↦Σ_i c_i x_i), a native integer linear-map kernel. It is the integral orthogonal of the native span_Z{c}.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: Apply native dotProductBilin over Z to c and take LinearMap.ker. Membership is the exact integer equation, with no primitivity hypothesis.
By symmetry and bilinearity, vanishing on c is equivalent to vanishing on its integral span. A nonzero scalar on c does not change the kernel because Z has no zero divisors.
The orthogonal-saturation theorem supplies saturation and complementary rank: if c≠0 then rank K(c)=N−1; if c=0 then K(c)=A_N.

nodes.title: Dot-product congruence kernel
nodes.statement: For c∈A_N and a natural Q let K_Q(c)=ker(A_N→ZMod Q, x↦Σ_i c_i x_i mod Q). Positive Q is the source modulus; the native extension Q=0 recovers the exact kernel.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: Compose the integer dot-product functional with native integer cast to ZMod Q and take LinearMap.ker. Use the pinned cast-zero/divisibility equivalence for membership.
For Q>0 the submodule contains QA_N and is full rank; its quotient identifies with the image of the residue functional.
To obtain its index API, diagonalize the integer row by the pinned PID theorem. Its image in Z is content(c)Z; modulo Q it has cardinal Q/gcd(content(c),Q). This includes c=0, when the index is one.

sources.match: Defines the modular incidence lattice and calculates simultaneous congruence indices. The single-row index and Q=0 convention are explicit worker extensions.

nodes.title: Gcd of maximal minors
nodes.statement: For every integer N×k matrix C let G(C) be the natural gcd of |det C_e| over all row embeddings e:Fin k→Fin N, where C_e uses every column in its original order. Reordered rows only duplicate absolute values. For k=0 the unique empty minor has determinant 1; for k>N there are no row embeddings and G(C)=0.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
No independence hypothesis belongs to this definition. In particular dependent positive-column matrices have G=0, a convention needed by p-adic consumers.
proofSteps: Use the existing Matrix submatrix/determinant and Finset.gcd over the finite set of embeddings. Normalization by integer absolute value removes signs and row-order choices.
The native gcd divisibility characterization supplies the universal property. The empty-column value is one, distinct from the empty-family value zero.

The minor-gcd-rank theorem proves the dependent-column convention. For a square right multiplier V, each selected minor of CV is C_e V; determinant multiplicativity and gcd_mul_right yield G(CV)=|det V|G(C).

sources.match: Defines G for independent columns; the total natural-valued extension is a worker API refinement required by the ArithmeticStatistics request.

acceptance: Do not confuse the gcd with a selected minor, its sign, or the determinant of the Gram matrix.

nodes.title: Unimodular invariance of determinantal content
nodes.statement: For any integer N×k C and integer unimodular N×N U, G(UC)=G(C). Combined with G(CV)=G(C)|det V|, this makes G invariant under unimodular changes in both ambient and generator coordinates.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
Unimodular means determinant is a unit in Z, hence ±1, not merely nonzero.
proofSteps: Expand each row of a selected minor of UC as an integer linear combination of rows of C. Repeated expansion by determinant row additivity and homogeneity expresses it as an integer combination of determinants of k-tuples of rows of C.
A tuple with a repeated row has determinant zero; a tuple of distinct rows is an embedding already included in G(C), up to row order. Thus G(C) divides every minor of UC and divides G(UC).

The integral inverse U⁻¹ gives the reverse divisibility. Natural gcd normalization gives equality. This supplies the minor-content argument that the read Le Boudec proof cites to Cassels; no rectangular Cauchy–Binet theorem is assumed.

sources.match: Worker replacement of the cited primitive-minor argument: integral row changes preserve the common divisor of maximal minors.

acceptance: A shear or orientation reversal leaves G unchanged. Multiplying one ambient coordinate by 2 is not a unimodular operation and can change G.

nodes.title: Vanishing content detects dependent columns
nodes.statement: For every integer N×k matrix C, G(C)=0 iff its rational columns are not linearly independent. Equivalently independent columns have positive G. This includes k=0 and k>N.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: The gcd is zero exactly when every selected maximal minor is zero. A nontrivial rational dependence survives selection of rows, so all selected square determinants vanish.

For independent columns, use the diagonal bases of the pinned PID inclusion for their column lattice in A_N. Its rank is k; every diagonal coefficient is nonzero. In these ambient coordinates the first k rows give the nonzero product of those coefficients times a unimodular generator determinant.
Unimodular invariance transfers nonvanishing content to the original matrix. Empty columns give G=1 and are independent; when k>N, independence is impossible and the minor family is empty.

sources.match: Worker extension of the independent-column definition, using its maximal minors to specify all boundary cases.

acceptance: Two equal columns give zero even if each column is primitive.
G for a nonzero single column is the gcd of its coordinates, hence positive.

nodes.title: Minor content is the saturation index
nodes.statement: If the k columns of integer N×k C are independent over Q and L=span_Z(columns C), then G(C)=[sat(L):L], the relative additive index of L in sat(L). This is a positive finite integer. For k=0 both sides are one; for k=N it is the full lattice index in A_N.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
Independence includes k=0 and implies k≤N. Dependent matrices do not satisfy this index formula with their maximal-column minors.
proofSteps: Diagonalize L≤A_N using the pinned PID theorem. Saturation-characterisation identifies sat(L) with the span of the first k ambient basis vectors.

The prescribed columns and the diagonal generators are both integral bases of L, so their generator-change matrix is unimodular. Apply the right determinant rule and ambient unimodular invariance to compute G(C)=product_i |a_i|.
Apply natAbs_det_basis_change in the intrinsic finite free module sat(L): the inclusion determinant is product_i a_i. Its absolute value is Nat.card(sat(L)/L), equal to the relative subgroup index.
This supplies the complete primitive-minor step in Le Boudec without using an unread Cassels reference or redeveloping Smith normal form.

sources.match: The read proof factors the columns through a saturation basis and identifies their maximal-minor gcd with the determinant of the inclusion.

acceptance: Columns 2e₁,3e₂ in Z³ have saturation index 6.
The primitive diagonal generator (1,1) has index and content one; (2,2) has both equal to two.

nodes.title: Covolume of simultaneous exact kernels
nodes.statement: For independent rational columns c₁,…,c_k of C (0≤k≤N), put L=span_Z(c_i) and H=⋂_i K(c_i)=L⊥. Then H is primitive of rank N−k and cov(H)=cov(L)/G(C). The source range 1≤k≤N−1 is included; the empty and full-column extensions have covolume one for the zero-dimensional side.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: The exact-kernel membership API identifies the intersection with the existing integral orthogonal of L. Orthogonal-saturation proves its rank and primitivity.
The accepted parent primitive-orthogonal-covolume identifies cov(H) with cov(sat(L)), in their respective real spans inside the standard self-dual ambient lattice.
Apply the pinned intrinsic covolume/relative-index theorem to L≤sat(L) in their common real span. The index theorem identifies the ratio with G(C); its positivity justifies division.
For k=0, L=0, H=A_N and G=1. For k=N, H=0 and the quotient is cov(L)/[A_N:L]=1. No ambient-volume calculation on a proper subspace is used.

sources.match: States the independent-column intersection determinant formula.
Supplies the saturation/inclusion determinant argument underlying Lemma 3.8.

acceptance: For columns 2e₁,3e₂ in Z³, the intersection is Ze₃ with covolume 1=6/6.

nodes.title: Primitive coefficient kernel covolume
nodes.statement: For a primitive integer vector c (gcd_i |c_i|=1), cov(K(c))=‖c‖₂. Such a vector is nonzero and N≥1. No corresponding equality is asserted for an unnormalized nonprimitive vector.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: Apply intersection-covolume to the single column c. Its integral line has intrinsic covolume ‖c‖₂ by the parent Gram identity, and its minor gcd is the coordinate gcd, one.

For a nonzero nonprimitive c, the same argument instead gives cov(K(c))=‖c‖₂/content(c). The zero coefficient vector has full kernel with covolume one and is handled by the definition API, not by division by its zero norm.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.8, p.11, k=1; Lemma 3.9 proof, p.12

nodes.title: Schmidt projected-dual equality
nodes.statement: If L≤A_N is primitive, W=span_R L, and π projects orthogonally onto W⊥, then the intrinsic inner dual of L⊥ in W⊥ equals π(A_N). Both sides are discrete full lattices in W⊥ of rank N−rank L. This is a concrete equality of submodules, not just an abstract group isomorphism.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
The dual lives in W⊥. The ambient dual of a lower-rank submodule in R^N is not used.
proofSteps: Use saturation-characterisation to identify L with A_N∩W. Apply the parent projected-adapted-basis to conclude π(A_N) is discrete and full in W⊥.
Standard A_N is self-dual for the coordinate inner pairing. The parent dual-projection-comap gives (π(A_N))*=L⊥ inside W⊥.

The pinned symmetric-nondegenerate double-dual theorem applies to the integral span of the projected real basis; dualizing again gives the stated equality. The parent orthogonal-intersection-basis supplies the rank/fullness of L⊥ independently.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.1 and definitions preceding it, p.8
sources.match: States the equality between the intrinsic dual of the integral orthogonal lattice and the projected quotient. The proof here terminates in the accepted parent projection bridge and pinned biduality rather than unread Schmidt.

acceptance: For L=Z(1,1), both sides are generated by (1/2,−1/2) in the antidiagonal line.
For L=A_N both sides are the zero lattice in dimension zero.
For L=0 both sides are the standard self-dual lattice.

nodes.title: Primitive-row triangular coordinates
nodes.statement: Let N≥2 and c,d∈A_N be independent over Q, with c primitive. There exist an integer unimodular N×N T and f∈Z for which cᵀT=(1,0,…,0) and dᵀT=(f,G(c,d),0,…,0), with G(c,d)>0. Primitivity of d is not required for this auxiliary result.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: Apply the pinned PID diagonalization to the row c, or to its transposed rank-one submodule. Coordinate content one makes its nonzero diagonal entry a unit; adjust its sign and transpose the integral coordinate change to obtain cᵀT₀=e₁ᵀ.
Write dᵀT₀=(f,v), with a nonzero residual integer row v by independence. A second PID row change inside the last N−1 coordinates takes v to (g,0,…,0), where g is its positive coordinate gcd.
The maximal 2×2 minors of the two transformed rows consist of the residual entries up to sign and zeros. Ambient unimodular invariance of the transposed column matrix identifies g with G(c,d).

Compose the two unimodular changes. This establishes the precise version of the source triangularization, retaining c as the first equation rather than silently applying row operations to both equations.

sources.match: The source introduces these coordinates. The two-step row argument spells out why the primitive first equation remains fixed.

acceptance: For c=(1,0), d=(1,2), T=identity, f=1 and G=2 work.
Replacing c by (2,0) violates the primitive hypothesis and cannot produce first row (1,0).

nodes.title: Two-congruence determinant
nodes.statement: Let N≥2, Q≥1, and primitive independent integer c,d. The full-rank lattice H=K_Q(c)∩K_Q(d) has index and intrinsic covolume [A_N:H]=cov(H)=Q²/gcd(G(c,d),Q). The fraction is an integer; full rank is a conclusion. The formula need not hold for dependent or nonprimitive pairs.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: Use pair-triangularisation with integer coordinates x=Tz. The first congruence is Q|z₁. With it imposed, the second is Q|Gz₂, because fz₁ is already divisible by Q.
Set g=gcd(G,Q). Elementary integer Bezout gives Q|Gz₂ iff (Q/g)|z₂. Thus in z-coordinates H has basis Qe₁,(Q/g)e₂,e₃,…,e_N.

Unimodular T preserves the additive index and full lattice covolume. The pinned determinant/index theorem gives Q(Q/g); the standard lattice has covolume one, and the pinned intrinsic ratio theorem identifies this index with cov(H).
The resulting positive finite index proves fullness. The original definitions also show QA_N≤H, making the conclusion independent of the calculation.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.9, first formula and proof (3.6)–(3.7), pp.11–12
sources.match: The two modular equations become diagonal divisibility conditions, yielding the full-rank determinant.

acceptance: c=(1,0), d=(1,2), Q=6 give G=2 and covolume 18, not 36.
For Q=1 every congruence kernel is A_N and the formula gives one.
For c=e₁,d=e₂ the index is Q².

nodes.title: Exact-and-congruence determinant
nodes.statement: Let N≥2, Q≥1, and primitive independent integer c,d. The lattice H=K(c)∩K_Q(d) has rank N−1 and intrinsic covolume cov(H)=‖c‖₂ Q/gcd(G(c,d),Q). More precisely [K(c):H]=Q/gcd(G(c,d),Q). H is a full lattice in the hyperplane c⊥; it need not be primitive in A_N.
hypotheses: N is a natural number, including zero; A_N=Z^N has its standard coordinate pairing. Integral submodules are finite free by the pinned PID theorem.
Real realizations use EuclideanSpace R (Fin N), not the supremum norm on an unweighted function space. cov(L) denotes canonical volume in span_R L, with cov(0)=1 in dimension zero.
proofSteps: In the same triangular coordinates, K(c) has basis Te₂,…,Te_N. The congruence on d becomes Q|Gz₂ since z₁=0.
With g=gcd(G,Q), the mixed lattice is generated by (Q/g)Te₂,Te₃,…,Te_N. Thus its relative index in K(c) is Q/g and its rank is N−1.

Apply the pinned covolume/relative-index theorem inside the real hyperplane c⊥, then substitute exact-kernel-covolume. T is generally not an isometry; no norm or Gram determinant is declared invariant under this integral coordinate change.
Unlike the full-rank congruence formula, this argument compares two lattices in their common hyperplane. Multiplying the complete kernel covolume by its relative index supplies the norm factor.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.9, second formula and proof, pp.11–12
sources.match: The exact first equation and residual modular condition give an index Q/g in the primitive exact kernel, hence the displayed determinant.

acceptance: c=(1,0), d=(1,2), Q=6 give H=3Ze₂ with covolume 3.
c=(1,1), d=(1,−1), Q=6 give H=3Z(1,−1) with intrinsic covolume 3√2.
For Q=1 the formula recovers cov(K(c))=‖c‖₂.
